title: Learning a Variational Network for Reconstruction of Accelerated MRI Data
layout_note: (a) Data processing pipeline: sensitivity-map stack (top left) and multi-coil k-space stack (bottom left) both feed an A* box that gives the zero-filled image, and both also run straight into a tall Variational Network box that outputs the reconstruction. (b) Below, the network as a row of GD^1 ... GD^t ... GD^T squares, with GD^t expanded by two trapezoid zoom lines into a large panel showing the gradient step.
grouping: One saturated dark green marks every learned unit (VN box, GD squares, A* box), against a white page; the expanded GD step sits in a pale olive-green square-cornered panel with a thin dark outline. Sub-figures are labelled (a)/(b) with captions below.
shapes_depth: Flat square-cornered boxes, the dark green ones with white serif text. Coil data are decks of offset stacked slices with tiny axis labels on their edges (n_FE, n_PE, n_CH; n_x, n_y); k-space is drawn as a dark image with vertical sampling lines. Inside the zoom panel the learned filters are small grey kernel thumbnails (real/imaginary pairs) and the activations are blue curve plots, joined by Σ nodes with +/- signs; the data term is an inline equation λ^t A*(A u^t − f) on its own arrow.
proposed_highlight: The whole network is one tall dark-green box bigger than every other element in (a), and its single repeated step is opened in (b) with zoom lines to show learned kernels and activation curves as pictures.
lesson: Coil data are drawn as decks of offset stacked slices with their array dimensions (n_FE, n_PE, n_CH) printed along the edges, so the multi-coil axis needs no legend.
notes: venue unverified: arXiv comment says 'Submitted to Magnetic Resonance in Medicine' (remembered as MRM 2018, not confirmed here); year = arXiv preprint year. All text is set in a serif (Computer Modern) face.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
